== Summary ==
[[Jan Siwanowicz]], faculty photo from the New York Math Circle's "In Memory of Jan Siwanowicz" entry. Photographer: unknown. 160 × 200 px, the size the site publishes.

== Source ==
* [https://www.nymathcircle.org/faculty NYMC - Faculty and Staff], New York Math Circle (retrieved 27 October 2026). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027202457/https://www.nymathcircle.org/faculty Internet Archive]. Image: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027202317/https://www.nymathcircle.org/static/photos/jan_siwanowicz.jpg jan_siwanowicz.jpg] (Wayback 27 October 2026; this file is that capture, SHA-256 1fa0d626d6ec1266c6d5a037e7773f9b80817a0f3ea0fe48c5d0e2f2125a1189).
* Match: the name is distinctive; the New York Math Circle entry describes a Polish mathematician (1994 IMO medalist for Poland) known for puzzles, and the 1997 Dagobah Contest winner of that name was from Warsaw.

== Fair use rationale ==
* '''Purpose:''' identifies the subject of the article [[Jan Siwanowicz]].
* '''Portion used:''' the whole image at the low resolution the site publishes.
* '''Replaceability:''' he died in 2023; no free photograph of him is known.
* '''Market effect:''' a small, non-commercial copy on a fan encyclopedia does not replace any commercial use.
* '''Copyright:''' the photographer or the New York Math Circle. Used under fair use for identification only.
